items.title: The ideal of divisible elements in a derived complete ring is nilpotent with an explicit bound
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A derived complete with respect to an ideal I, sets J equal to the intersection of the ideals I^n, and asserts that if I can be generated by r elements then J^N = 0 where N = 2^r (source lines 27106-27111). The proof is an induction on the number of generators. The case r = 1 is the square-zero statement (proof line 27114). For r > 1 write I = (f_1, ..., f_r); by the Serre subcategory statement the ring A_t = A/f_r^t A is derived complete with respect to I, hence a fortiori derived complete with respect to I_t = (f_1, ..., f_{r-1})A_t (proof lines 27115-27119). The map A -> A_t sends J into J_t = intersection of the ideals I_t^n (proof lines 27119-27120). By induction on r one has J_t^{N/2} = 0, where N = 2^r (proof lines 27120-27121). Finally the ideal given by the intersection of the kernels of A -> A_t, which is the intersection of the ideals f_r^t A, has square zero by the case r = 1, which finishes the proof (proof lines 27121-27122). The non-routine content is the doubling bookkeeping: the induction gives the exponent 2^{r-1} on the quotient, the square-zero statement contributes exponent 2 on the kernel, and the product of the two exponents is 2^r. The proof is terse and does not spell out the filtration argument combining J_t^{N/2} = 0 with the square-zero statement.
